Hai all,
Today we are discussing about integral mathematics.

In mathematics, an integral is a fundamental concept used to calculate areas, volumes, and accumulated quantities, and it represents the continuous analog of a sum.
An integral is either a numerical value representing the area under a curve (definite integral) or a function whose derivative is the original function (indefinite integral).
The definite integral computes the signed area between a function and the x-axis over a specific interval, with areas above the axis considered positive and areas below negative.
The indefinite integral, also called an antiderivative, is a function that, when differentiated, returns the original function.
Integration is the process of finding an integral and is one of the two central operations in calculus, alongside differentiation.
Conceptually, integration can be thought of as summing infinitely small slices of a function to find the total area or accumulated quantity.
The integral symbol ∫ represents this summation, followed by the integrand (the function to integrate) and dx, indicating the variable of integration.
Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
The fundamental theorem of calculus connects differentiation and integration, stating that if a function has an antiderivative, the definite integral over an interval can be computed using this antiderivative.
This theorem allows integrals to be evaluated efficiently without summing infinitely many slices manually.
